problem:
For the piecewise function 

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}-x\, & \text{ for }\,x\le -1 \\ x+c\, & \text{ for }\,x>-1\end{aligned}
$$

it is known that ${lim}_{x\to -1}f(x)=1.$ What is the value of the constant $c?$

feedback.worked_solution:
In order for ${lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)$ to be equal to $4,$ the left and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal to $4.$

- Approaching from the left, we have $-3\le x<1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=a{x}^{2}-3x+2.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}(a{x}^{2}-3x+2) \\  & =a({1}^{2})-3(1)+2 \\  & =a-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the left-sided limit must be equal to $4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x) & =4 \\ a-1 & =4 \\ a & =4+1 \\ a & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

- Approaching from the right, we have $1\le x\le 3,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=3{x}^{2}-bx.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}(3{x}^{2}-bx) \\  & =3({1}^{2})-b(1) \\  & =3-b\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the right-sided limit must be equal to $4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & =4 \\ 3-b & =4 \\ b & =3-4 \\ b & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
